item.title: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him in awful loss to UCLA
item.description: Dylan Raiola went 6-19 with two interceptions before being benched as the Oregon Ducks committed seven turnovers in a stunning home loss to UCLA.
item.content:encoded:
This was supposed to be the year.

The Oregon Ducks started the 2026 college football season as a consensus top-five team under head coach Dan Lanning. They brought back Dante Moore and added Dylan Raiola, a former starter at Nebraska, as a backup quarterback. They had a highly-paid roster full of former top recruits, along with impactful transfer portal additions. They were coming off back-to-back College Football Playoff appearances with a combined 26-3 record across the regular and postseason in 2024-2025.

Some suggested it was the best team Oregon's ever had. Almost immediately, however, the Ducks started taking on water. Boise State nearly pulled off the upset in Eugene in week one. Then Oklahoma State finished their upset bid in week two behind a dominant offensive performance.

DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA

After an 84-0 shellacking of Portland State, the Ducks went into Los Angeles for a pivotal game against USC at the Coliseum and finally seemed to turn the corner. When Moore left the game after an awful hit from a USC linebacker, Raiola stepped up and looked even better. Moore went 19-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns, helping secure a 41-27 win to seemingly save Oregon's season.

Lanning took the opportunity after the win to make a statement about the Ducks' program and where their focus lies.

"I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon," Lanning said, referring to high school players from the Los Angeles and Southern California area. "If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here."

Fast-forward two weeks and Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him.

The Ducks on Saturday hosted UCLA under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins, after years of mediocrity, have looked dramatically improved thus far in 2026, though against overmatched opponents like Cal, Purdue, and Maryland. Saturday marked their first test, a road game in one of the toughest environments in college football, against a team with aspirations of reaching and winning the College Football Playoff.

For Lanning, it was an opportunity to back up his statement, that if you want to play winning football, you come to Oregon. They lost.

The Ducks played one of the sloppiest games from any program in recent memory, somehow managing to turn the ball over an incredible seven times. They had five lost fumbles, and recovered the ball on a sixth fumble. Raiola was so awful, going 6-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions, that Lanning benched him for third stringer Brock Thomas.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Oregon's first quarter on offense was remarkable. Four plays for 22 yards and a punt, a one-yard touchdown drive after a Nico Iamaleava fumble, three plays for zero yards, and four plays for 20. 12 plays for 43 yards, and it got worse from there. Much worse.

Here's the drive chart for Oregon's second quarter:

16 plays for 25 yards, two punts, two fumbles, and an interception.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Ducks did pick up more yards in the third quarter though, going three plays for two yards, four plays for 22 yards and a fumble, and two plays for seven yards and another pick. That's 31 total yards and only two turnovers instead of three. Progress!

While Oregon did have a better run in the fourth quarter, working around another fumble to kick a field goal and finally score their second touchdown of the game with 2:16 remaining, the two-point conversion attempt to tie the score at 17-17 failed.

Fittingly, the game ended on Oregon fumbling while trying to run a series of laterals down the field as time expired. As Lanning said, "If you care about winning games, and you're from LA, come to Oregon." Or apparently UCLA.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

It's hard to imagine an uglier game and result, for any team, let alone one that started the season in the top-5 with realistic hopes of winning a National Championship. Obviously, Moore being out hurt the Ducks' offense, but seven turnovers? Only 272 yards, at home, against a UCLA team that unquestionably has inferior talent?

At one point, Oregon went six straight drives without picking up a first down. At one point, excluding the end of the second quarter, the Ducks turned the ball over on six out of nine drives. That is ... remarkable.

From 2023-2025, Lanning built Oregon into one of the most consistent teams in the country. They were 38-5, and went undefeated in their first season in the Big Ten to secure the number one overall seed in the 2024-2025 playoff. For most of that run, his teams were seen as well coached and disciplined.

Yet it's impossible to watch a team commit seven turnovers and lose a game, at home, in that fashion, and come away with the impression that they're well coached. How the USC game played out the way it did seems to be a serious indictment of the job Lincoln Riley and Gary Patterson did in Los Angeles. But for recruits or the unfortunate fans at Autzen Stadium, maybe they should have gone to a Chris Brown concert instead.

item.title: Gas stations may be hiding some of America's most overlooked affordable fast-food options
item.description: From Wawa's hoagies to Buc-ee's chopped brisket, these convenience store and gas station meals can be surprisingly delicious budget-friendly meals. Check out this list.
item.content:encoded:
Some people may shy away from the idea of getting a meal at a gas station or convenience store — but doing so could be an easy, and surprisingly delicious, way to save money while on a road trip or during a daily commute.

Restaurant menu prices rose 0.3% in both July and August this year, and menu prices were 3.4% higher this August than in August 2025, the National Restaurant Association reported in September. 

"Gas stations with quick service attached to them like 7Eleven, am/pm, etc. are the real value now," a Reddit user said in a recent thread. 

FAST-FOOD DRIVE-THRUS TOOK OVER AMERICAN MORNINGS FOR THESE KEY REASONS

"Everything has shifted upwards. Fast food is now fast casual pricing. Fast casual is now sit down restaurant pricing."

Amid these increases, finding inexpensive and convenient dining options might be challenging, but it’s not impossible.

Here are a few convenience store and gas station chains offering tasty, budget-friendly meals and snacks — ranging from a $5 half-foot-long sub sandwich to a $9.99 box filled to the brim with Southern comfort food. 

New Jersey-based gas station and convenience chain QuickChek has more than 160 locations across New Jersey and parts of New York.

Six-inch subs and sandwiches cost $5 a piece, while a $4 breakfast combo includes an English muffin or croissant breakfast sandwich and a 20-ounce hot coffee or energy drink, according to the website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The chain also offers a small, medium or large iced coffee for $1.99, which includes any customizations.

Headquartered in Pennsylvania, Wawa serves coffee, a variety of breakfast items, snacks and freshly made sandwiches.

The chain earned the top spot in the American Customer Satisfaction Index’s 2024 convenience store ranking primarily due to the chain’s food offerings, especially its hoagies.

A classic Italian hoagie on a six-inch roll costs $6.29, while a breakfast meal including a breakfast sandwich, a hash brown and a coffee or fountain drink costs $5, according to the Wawa website.

Since its founding in 1982, Beaver-themed gas station chain Buc-ee’s has developed a reputation for affordable gas prices, logo-adorned merchandise, and its extensive food offerings.

The lower gas prices are mainly due to the fact that customers are expected to spend more money inside the store, Yahoo Finance reported in June.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

The chopped brisket sandwich is a popular grab-and-go meal option, with the standard 8-ounce size selling for less than $10 at most locations, according to a website sharing Buc-ee’s menu items and pricing information.

Some Redditors say that a trip to Buc-ee’s is not complete without Beaver nuggets, a sweet, crunchy puffed corn snack. A large bag of Beaver nuggets sells for about five dollars, and the homemade fudge costs about four dollars per square, according to Southern Living.

All Buc-ee’s locations are open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, according to the website, and as an added bonus, the restrooms are known for being extremely sanitary.

In a Buc-ee’s thread on Reddit, a commenter said, "Be sure to check out the clean bathrooms!"

Founded in Georgia in 1976, Parker’s Kitchen operates 110 locations across Georgia and South Carolina.

Known for Southern-inspired food like fried chicken and biscuits, the gas station and convenience chain offers meal options with prices that rival those at fast-food restaurants.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

A $9.99 Fill Up Box from Parker’s Kitchen includes a small side, a drink, and the choice of three chicken tenders, a chicken sandwich, two pork chops, two pieces of fried catfish, or livers and gizzards.

The lunch menu features a $4.99 pulled pork sandwich and a $3.99 barbecue chicken sandwich, as well as a $3.99 cheeseburger, according to the website.

item.title: Daughters of the American Revolution axes chapter that challenged transgender membership
item.description: DAR's National Board voted to disband the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas, which led efforts to block transgender women from joining the organization.
item.content:encoded:
The Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR) voted Saturday to disband its Martha Laird Chapter in Texas that fought to bar transgender women from joining the historic organization, citing violations of its national bylaws.

In a letter to chapter members, DAR Organizing Secretary General Marguerite Hogan Fritsch announced that the National Board of Management had approved the chapter's dissolution by a two-thirds majority vote.

"On October 10, 2026, at the meeting of the National Board of Management of the National Society, Daughters of the American Revolution a resolution passed by two-thirds majority vote to disband the Martha Laird Chapter, NSDAR," Fritsch said in the letter. "The actions of the chapter have been found in violation of Article XIX, Section 4 of the Bylaws of the National Society Daughters of the American Revolution," the letter continued.

The letter did not identify the specific conduct that constituted a violation or state whether the chapter's opposition to transgender membership contributed to the decision. 

SORORITY ALUMNAE TAKE LEGAL FIGHT TO FEDERAL COURT AFTER BEING 'GIVEN A BROTHER' INSTEAD OF SISTERHOOD

The National Society Daughters of the American Revolution confirmed to Fox News Digital that the organization had voted to disband the local Texas chapter but denied it was due to its views on membership.
 
 "The National Board of Management voted on October 10 to disband the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas after finding that chapter officers had used the chapter’s name, leadership positions, communications, and governance processes to further the goals of a separate advocacy organization," the group told Fox News Digital. "The Board determined that it was this use of chapter authority and resources – not the views being advocated – that constituted conduct discrediting the National Society under Article XIX, Section 4 of the National Bylaws."

 "The Board’s decision was not based on the chapter’s or its members’ views concerning membership eligibility, their efforts to propose changes to the National Bylaws, or their right to advocate for changes in National Society governance," the statement continued.

The group noted that at their June 2026 meeting, national members had rejected a resolution to add further membership restrictions. Individual members of the Texas chapter retain their DAR membership and are free to advocate for changes to the National Bylaws through the Society’s established governance processes, the organization said.

ALL-WOMEN'S SCHOOL WELLESLEY COLLEGE RESPONDS TO ACCUSATIONS OF ADMITTING BIOLOGICAL MALE TRANS STUDENTS

The chapter previously challenged DAR leadership's position on transgender membership, with member Laura McDonald telling Fox News Digital last year that the organization was contradicting its founding mission by recognizing transgender women as eligible members.

"But, then they go on to say that a man who claims he's a woman is a woman, and therefore he's eligible for membership. But if you are a man that doesn't claim to be a woman, you're not eligible for membership," McDonald said.

Conservative California superintendent candidate Sonja Shaw told Fox News Digital that women and girls are being told that spaces created to protect their privacy, dignity, and opportunities "no longer belong to them," including sports, restrooms, locker rooms, and now, according to her, the Daughters of the American Revolution.

"The women of the Martha Laird Chapter in Texas stood their ground. They sought to preserve a definition of "Daughters" based on biological sex and asked for a clear vote. On October 10, national leadership dissolved their chapter," Shaw said. 

SMITH COLLEGE 'MAKES A MOCKERY' OF ALL-WOMEN STATUS BY ADMITTING TRANSGENDER STUDENTS, EDUCATION WATCHDOG SAYS

"Think about that. Women who stood up for their convictions saw their chapter, with a history dating back to 1942, dissolved. Here is the damning question national leadership needs to answer: Why should women be punished for standing up for the very definition of the organization they belong to?" she added. 

Shaw also pointed to similar debates across the country concerning sports and privacy in women's spaces, and said "this is about more than one chapter."

"Our daughters deserve a future where they never have to ask permission to stand up for the truth, and where no woman is punished for having the courage to speak it," Shaw said.

Under DAR's national bylaws, Article XIX, Section 4 authorizes the National Board of Management to discipline or disband chapters that violate organizational rules or engage in conduct that discredits the DAR.

The dissolution comes nearly three months after Rep. Ben Cline, R-Va., introduced the Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act, which would amend DAR's congressional charter to restrict membership to biological women. 

Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., subsequently introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

"Rather than honoring and preserving a lineage-based organization for women, it has embraced radical gender ideology at the expense of the women it was created to serve," Cline said.

In September 2024, the Martha Laird Chapter, supported by 11 other chapters, submitted a proposed bylaw amendment defining membership eligibility based on biological sex.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The Center for American Liberty also provided legal assistance to the chapter, challenging DAR leadership's contention that excluding transgender applicants could jeopardize the organization's tax-exempt status.

The proposed amendment was rejected by DAR's National Board of Management in February 2025. McDonald criticized the decision at the time.

"The rejection by the National Board of Management of our proposal to define a woman in our bylaws sadly confirms what we knew all along – that leadership is taking a political stance which is not based on fears of the loss of 501(c)(3) nonprofit status," McDonald said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

DAR, founded in 1890, previously maintained that its longstanding membership policies allowed women with legally amended birth certificates to join, provided they otherwise met the organization's genealogical requirements.

Under the dissolution notice, Martha Laird Chapter members will be transferred to member-at-large status and have until Nov. 9 to secure acceptance into another chapter. The letter also directed that dues previously remitted to the chapter be refunded.

item.title: Week 6 AP Top 25 poll sees a major mixup and a new top team in the country after an upset-filled Saturday
item.description: Georgia claims the No. 1 spot in the AP Poll after its stunning road win over Alabama, while Kentucky vaults from unranked to No. 15 in Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
Every college football Saturday is a memorable one, but some weekends deliver more drama than others, and Week 6 certainly falls into that category after the upsets that took place all around the country.

The shuffling of teams in the Week 6 AP Poll reflects the madness that unfolded, including Georgia picking up arguably the most impressive win of the season after taking down Alabama in Tuscaloosa. The Bulldogs were rewarded by taking over the No. 1 spot in the rankings. Texas, the No. 1 team in the nation since Week 2, fell six spots after being stunned at the Cotton Bowl by unranked Oklahoma.

The biggest movers in the latest AP Poll were two teams that faced off against one another on Saturday, with Kentucky going from unranked to No. 15 after stunning LSU in overtime. Lane Kiffin's Tigers dropped 12 spots all the way to No. 22 after falling to 4-2 on the year.

KIRBY SMART HAS ENTERED HIS MOST DANGEROUS ERA AFTER GEORGIA’S AGGRESSIVE WIN OVER ALABAMA

Welcome letters are in order for Northwestern, Wake Forest, and Kentucky, as all three teams enter the Top 25 after being unranked a week ago. Oregon, after its home loss to UCLA, and Florida, after being blown out at home by South Carolina, both exited the polls, after both the Ducks and Gators were ranked inside the Top 16 in Week 5.

INDIANA SURVIVES NEBRASKA IN COMEBACK WIN, EXTENDS NATION'S LONGEST ACTIVE WINNING STREAK

While the No. 1 next to Georgia's name is the ultimate sign of respect from voters, it's also worth noting that Alabama remained at No. 6 despite losing to the Bulldogs in its first dropped game of the year. It's clear that voters are impressed by Kirby Smart's squad in Athens.

The new No. 2 team in the nation, Notre Dame, gets its first test of the season in Week 7 when it travels to take on No. 8 BYU on the road.

Other notable games in Week 7 include No. 4 Ohio State visiting No. 5 Indiana, No. 9 Ole Miss hosting No. 13 Missouri, No. 6 Alabama traveling to No. 14 Tennessee, No. 15 Kentucky visiting Oklahoma, No. 22 LSU welcoming No. 16 Mississippi State to Baton Rouge, plus No. 20 Houston hosting No. 18 Oklahoma State.

The Week 7 slate is a loaded one, which means more chaos and movement in next week's polls is inevitable.

item.title: Bill Gates sounds alarm on AI-powered cyberattacks, warns of 'negative surprises' within a year
item.description: Bill Gates warned that AI-powered cyberattacks could disrupt financial systems and fuel extortion schemes, with criminals exploiting unsafeguarded models.
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates warned Sunday that artificial intelligence could fuel a wave of cyberattacks over the next year, and said that malicious actors are gaining access to increasingly powerful AI models without adequate safeguards.

Gates warned that criminals could exploit the latest AI technology to disrupt financial systems, extort businesses and carry out increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.

"When you have bad people, no safeguards, and then the latest models, that's where, over the next year, primarily in the cyber area, we are going to have a lot of negative surprises," Gates said during a "State of the Union" interview with CNN's Jake Tapper.

BILL GATES WARNS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE 'POWERFUL ENOUGH' TO CAUSE 'A BILLION DEATHS' IF UNCHECKED

Democratic strategist Oliver Libby told Fox News Digital that Gates' warning underscores the challenge facing policymakers as artificial intelligence advances and the United States seeks to maintain its technological competitiveness.

"The great challenge both for innovators and governments in the coming months is to balance continued progress in AI with smart regulation. Leaders who can balance ensuring that America is not left behind, but that no American is left out, will win public trust," Libby said.

Gates' warning comes as cybersecurity researchers report a sharp increase in AI-enabled threats. 

According to CrowdStrike's 2026 Global Threat Report, attacks by AI-enabled adversaries increased 89% year over year in 2025, while the average time for cybercriminals to move laterally through compromised networks fell to 29 minutes.

WATCH: AI SAFETY SCARE SPARKS CAP HILL FIGHT OVER GUARDRAILS: 'CHINA'S GOING TO EAT OUR LUNCH'

Tapper pressed Gates about his warning that artificial intelligence could make it easier for terrorists to develop deadly biological weapons, citing his assessment that the risk of a bioterrorist attack could become 50 times greater than that of a natural pandemic. 

Tapper also questioned how soon such an attack could occur and whether government leaders were doing enough to prevent it.

"Well, no, we're not doing enough," Gates said. "The real danger right now is not the AI is getting out of control. We need to work on that, but that's years away in terms of the big impact that might have."

BIOWEAPON THREAT EXPOSED AS ANTHROPIC SOUNDS ALARM ON FOREIGN ACTORS PLOTTING VIRUS EXPERIMENTS

Gates described potential financial motivations behind cyberattacks, including extortion schemes and disruptions designed to manipulate financial markets or betting outcomes.

"The front that we'll probably see most dramatically in the next year is cyberattacks, because there, there's a known business model where, you know, you threaten to do something and ask somebody to pay for that, or you create a disruption that changes something in the stock market or some betting thing that you go and do," Gates said.

Libby called for a coordinated regulatory approach that addresses security risks while preparing Americans for AI's broader economic consequences.

"Regulation should focus on federal and international standards, platform responsibility, cyber and deepfake penalties, child safety, and ensuring the participation of the population in the economic benefits of this powerful technological revolution — while starting to prepare our society for what could be profound workforce disruption," Libby said.

item.title: Mike Ditka tributes pour in from around the NFL including fans dressing like him in Green Bay
item.description: Fans in Green Bay donned classic Mike Ditka costumes with sweaters, mustaches, and cigars as the Packers held a moment of silence before kickoff.
item.content:encoded:
Imitation is considered a great form of flattery and, in the case of former Chicago Bears coach Mike Ditka, it has become a tribute since his passing on Friday at the age of 86.

On Sunday when the Bears were playing the Packers, multiple fans showed up to the game wearing Ditka costumes.

In Green Bay.

LEGENDARY BEARS COACH MIKE DITKA DEAD AT AGE 86

Multiple fans showed up wearing the classic 1980s-style Bears sweater, the Ditka-style mustaches (some of them fake), the sunglasses, and holding cigars in their mouths.

It wasn't mockery.

It was a memoriam.

All this because that was the Ditka look everyone remembers, Saturday Night Live many times spoofed, and NFL films saluted.

TRUMP GIVES RAW REACTION AFTER FINDING OUT ABOUT MIKE DITKA'S DEATH: 'A TOUGH COOKIE'

Before the game between the Packers and Bears, two teams that share a rivalry dating to 1921, the Packers showed their class by showing their opponents great respect in memory of Ditka.

With the University of Wisconsin band on the field at attention, the Packers remembered Ditka.

"Ladies and gentlemen, the Green Bay Packers and the NFL community are saddened to learn of the passing of Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka," the public address announcement echoed. "We extend our sincere condolences to his family, friends, and the entire Chicago Bears organization.

"At this time please join in a moment of silence."

That moment of silence came to an end with a round of applause from the crowd – a fan base that once upon a time wanted very badly to beat Ditka in what both franchises call the greatest rivalry of all time.

The New Orleans Saints, which Ditka coached from 1997-99, similarly held a moment of silence before their home game against the Minnesota Vikings.

Bears players are wearing No. 89 helmet decals honoring Ditka’s retired Bears number on Sunday.

Bears coach Ben Johnson also reportedly showed the team a Ditka tribute video during a meeting Saturday night.

In Chicago, fans gathered at Ditka’s Oak Brook restaurant, and a local business organized Ditka trivia and signed-jersey giveaways.

All the networks broadcasting NFL games on Sunday have paid tribute to Ditka.

The Bears on Friday lowered their flag to half-staff at Halas Hall, displayed a memorial image outside Soldier Field and called Ditka’s impact "immeasurable."

Coach Ben Johnson said Ditka was "the gold standard" and that he felt humbled to occupy the same chair.

And all this is honorable and notable. But, to me, it is the fans dressing like Ditka who offer the most lasting and impressive tribute.

These people decide they are going to dress themselves, and sometimes their children, to look like Ditka. They might even join a group of friends who do the same. It takes effort to do that. It takes forethought and planning.

And it is all a statement of appreciation and admiration.

item.title: Jaguars kicker sticks it to Eagles fans after nailing game-winning 57-yard field goal in London
item.description: Cam Little's 57-yard field goal stunned the Eagles after Ameer Abdullah's kickoff return set up the Jacksonville Jaguars for a dramatic finish.
item.content:encoded:
There’s nothing sweeter than an early-morning NFL game that goes down to the wire and leads you right into the afternoon kickoff.

The Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles blessed us with that on Sunday. The game, while mostly sloppy from the start, saw the Jaguars and Eagles trade scores in the fourth quarter. Trevor Lawrence found Parker Washington on fourth down to take the lead with 3:20 left in the game. Then, Eagles kicker Jake Elliott gave Philly a one-point lead with eight seconds left.

Philadelphia, for whatever reason, thought it was a good idea to boot the ball to a Jaguars returner instead of kicking it into the end zone and hoping Lawrence could chuck up a prayer to win the game. Ameer Abdullah broke away from Philadelphia’s special teams and got the ball across midfield and into Eagles territory with one second left.

Jaguars kicker Cam Little nailed a game-winning 57-yard field goal. Jacksonville took home the 19-17 victory and moved to 4-1 on the season.

Little immediately ran back toward the opposite end zone and taunted some of the Eagles fans who lined the barrier. Little’s kick probably would have been good from about 70 yards. His teammates lifted him up in celebration.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Eagles fell to 2-3 with the loss.

The game was chaotic from the beginning. Jaguars rookie returner Josh Cameron thought he had a 90-yard kickoff return touchdown from the jump. It would have been the first kickoff-return TD in the NFL this year. Offsetting penalties nullified the return.

On the same play, Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jaguars blocker Bryan Thomas Jr. got into a scuffle and were kicked out of the game. It certainly was a "crackers" start to the game, as OutKick’s Armando Salguero wrote this morning.

Despite having 13 penalties for 100 yards, Jacksonville was able to escape London with the dub.
